name: eshkol
description: High-Performance LISP-like language for Scientific Computing and AI written in C++

paragraphs: Eshkol is a Scheme-based programming language that unifies functional programming with native automatic differentiation, providing a mathematically rigorous foundation for gradient-based optimization, numerical simulation, and machine learning. Built on Homotopy Type Theory foundations and compiled to native code via LLVM, Eshkol delivers mathematical correctness and deterministic performance without sacrificing the elegance of homoiconic Lisp syntax.

Prepared for publication: v1.3.6-evolve. Intended release date: Thursday, October 15, 2026. Source-bound preparation passed all 823 configured CTest cases and all 411 VM parity cases. Publication requires exact-commit release evidence and an ICC ready/100 verdict. See the latest published release, release notes and upgrading guide.
Full documentation index — every guide, reference, and design doc in one place.

Native compilation - LLVM backend generates machine code competitive with hand-written C while preserving high-level expressiveness
